profile.summary: Protein-RAG is a family of retrieval-augmented protein language models from GenBio AI, published under the names AIDO.Protein-RAG and AIDO.RAGPLM and now served as GB.Protein-RAG. Each model takes a protein sequence together with a retrieved multiple sequence alignment of homologues and, in the larger versions, per-residue structure embeddings, and it predicts masked residues. The embeddings and logits are used for contact prediction, structure prediction and fitness prediction. The models are released on Hugging Face and run through the ModelGenerator framework.
profile.summary_source_locator: 16B card: introduction; 3B card: introduction; preprint abstract

summary_quotes.text: GB.Protein-RAG-16B is a multimodal protein language model that integrates Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA) and structural data, building upon the [GB.Protein-16B](https://huggingface.co/genbio-ai/GB.Protein-16B) foundation.

integrates pretrained protein language models with retrieved Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSA), enabling the incorporation of co-evolutionary information for structure prediction while compensating for limited MSA data through large-scale pretraining.
AIDO.RAGPLM integrates pre-trained protein language models with retrieved MSA, surpassing single-sequence protein language models in perplexity, contact prediction, and fitness prediction.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The models are transformer encoders trained with masked language modelling on a query sequence concatenated with its retrieved homologues. Two-dimensional rotary position embeddings let the model tell which chain a token belongs to and which residue index it holds. Masking is applied by column: when a residue of the query is selected, the aligned residues in every homologue are masked too, which stops the answer leaking from the alignment. The 16B models add structure: per-residue embeddings of dimension 384, produced by GenBio's structure tokenizer, are projected to the model width and added to the query token embeddings, and the loss is a weighted sum of a sequence term and a structure term. The 3B model uses dense MLP blocks; the 16B models replace them with sparse mixture-of-experts layers that route each token to two experts.

quotes.text: GB.Protein-RAG-16B employs a transformer encoder-only architecture featuring sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers that replace dense MLP layers in each transformer block.
When a residue is selected, its aligned residues across all sequences (MSA column) are also masked.
Structure embeddings (dim = 384) are linearly mapped to 2304 and added to the query token embeddings.
Total loss is a weighted sum of sequence loss (weight 1.0) and structure loss (weight 0.01).
GB.Protein-RAG-3B employs a transformer encoder-only architecture with dense MLP layers in each block

We fine-tuned a pretrained masked language model with 3-billion parameters ([MLM-3B](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.06.06.597716v1)) using MSA data by concatenating the query sequence with homologous sequences.
the model activates 2 experts per token via top-2 routing mechanisms.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Three checkpoints are published: GB.Protein-RAG-3B, GB.Protein-RAG-16B and GB.Protein-RAG-16B-proteingym-dms-zeroshot. The 3B model is the one the preprint names; it was fine-tuned from a 3-billion-parameter masked language model on 100 billion tokens of alignment data. The 16B model was built from GB.Protein-16B in three stages: position embedding fine-tuning on 10 billion tokens, 100 billion tokens of UniRef50 and UniClust30 alignments, then 80 billion tokens of AlphaFold Database alignments and structure tokens. The zero-shot checkpoint follows the same recipe but with 23 billion tokens in the third stage and a structure loss weight of 0.025 instead of 0.01. The models were first published under AIDO names; the old Hugging Face address for the 3B model now serves the repository named GB.Protein-RAG-3B, and the ModelGenerator backbone registry maps aido_protein_rag_16b and aido_protein_rag_3b to the gb_ names. A result should name the checkpoint, its revision and the backbone name used.

sections.title: Licence and access
sections.body: Everything GenBio publishes on these pages, code, weights and datasets, is covered by the GenBio AI Community License Agreement, which permits non-commercial use only and forbids using the outputs to train similar models. The Hugging Face licence field reads 'other'. The checkpoints are not gated. The ModelGenerator repository, which holds the backbone definitions and the ProteinGym experiment configs, states that it is deprecated and kept for the previous generation of models.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Retrieval-augmented protein language model: a masked language model over a query sequence with its retrieved alignment, and for the 16B models also with structure embeddings.

quotes.text: GB.Protein-RAG-16B is a multimodal protein language model that integrates Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA) and structural data, building upon the [GB.Protein-16B](https://huggingface.co/genbio-ai/GB.Protein-16B) foundation.
AIDO.RAGPLM integrates pre-trained protein language models with retrieved MSA, surpassing single-sequence protein language models in perplexity, contact prediction, and fitness prediction.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Transformer encoder with 2D rotary position embeddings. The 16B models: 36 layers, 36 attention heads, hidden size 2304, FFN size 7680, 8 mixture-of-experts layers per block with 2 experts active per token, vocabulary 44. The 3B model: 36 layers, 40 heads, hidden size 2560, FFN size 6832, dense MLP blocks.

facts.value: A protein sequence, a multiple sequence alignment of homologues (the usage example passes 25 aligned sequences), and for the 16B models per-residue structure embeddings of dimension 384 from GenBio's structure tokenizer.

"""GB.Protein-RAG model with 3B parameters adapted from a 3B version of GB.Protein 16B with 180B tokens of MSA and structural context from UniRef50/UniClust30 and AlphaFold Database.

We fine-tuned a pretrained masked language model with 3-billion parameters ([MLM-3B](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.06.06.597716v1)) using MSA data by concatenating the query sequence with homologous sequences.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: UniRef50 queries with UniClust30 homologues found by HHblits (23.7 million alignments) plus 7.7 million more from the MSA Retriever, sampled 0.75 to 0.25; and, for the 16B models, 46.9 million sequence and structure pairs from the AlphaFold Database, filtered on pLDDT and clustered at 50% identity. Stage 1 reuses the ColabFoldDB and UniRef data of the base model.

quotes.text: Using HHblits, we searched all sequences, identifying over 25 homologous sequences for 23.7 million of them.
This dataset was designated as `Retriever_MSA`. During training, RAGPLM randomly sampled from the two datasets with probabilities of 0.75 and 0.25.
We downloaded all structural data from the AlphaFold Database and kept only those where more than 40% of amino acids had a pLDDT score > 70.

run_guide.summary: Install ModelGenerator and get embeddings from GB.Protein-RAG-16B for one sequence with an alignment and structure embeddings.
prerequisites: Python 3.10, 3.11 or 3.12, as the README's badge states.
A GPU. The sources read give no memory figure, so the hardware needed is unknown; the card's own snippets move the model to cuda.
An alignment for the query sequence, and per-residue structure embeddings of dimension 384, which the card says come from GenBio's structure tokenizer.
Code and weights are under the GenBio AI Community License Agreement, which allows non-commercial use only.

steps.title: Get embeddings for one sequence
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import random
import numpy as np
import torch
from modelgenerator.tasks import Embed

model = Embed.from_config({"model.backbone": "gb_protein_rag_16b"}).eval()
model.backbone.max_length = 12800
restypes = 'ARNDCQEGHILKMFPSTWYV'
data = {
    'sequences': [''.join(random.choice(restypes) for _ in range(50))],
    'msa': [ [ ''.join(random.choice(restypes+'-') for _ in range(50)) for _ in range(25) ] ],
    'str_emb': np.random.normal(size=(1, 50, 384))
}
transformed_batch = model.transform(data)
with torch.no_grad():
    embedding = model(transformed_batch)

print(embedding.shape)
PY
steps.explanation: The card's embedding snippet, wrapped in a shell heredoc. Two changes: the imports of random and numpy are added, because the card's snippet uses them without importing them, and the backbone name is the registry's current gb_protein_rag_16b rather than the card's older aido_protein_rag_16b, which the registry maps to it. The msa and str_emb values here are random, as in the card: replace them with a real alignment and real structure embeddings. For the 3B model use gb_protein_rag_3b.
